nodes.label: Use SMS_STS, Never SCSCL
nodes.rationale: SCSCL is the SC series and its register map differs: mode is at address 19 there, 33 here.

nodes.label: Vendored Arduino Libraries
nodes.rationale: Patched Ethernet and SCServo live in libraries/ and are referenced by sketch.yaml so nothing is fetched at build time. The folder name must match the sketch.yaml entry.

nodes.label: Dev And Test Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Adds pytest, pytest-cov and httpx on top of the runtime set.

nodes.label: Runtime Dependencies
nodes.rationale: fastapi, uvicorn and pydantic-settings only; a deliberately small surface for an air-gapped wheelhouse.

nodes.label: Six-Fault Status Grid
nodes.rationale: Overload, Current, Heat, Voltage, Sensor and Angle tiles mirroring the six decoded status flags.

nodes.label: Angle And Speed Move Controls
nodes.rationale: Typed text inputs with 0.06 degree nudge steps for angle and 5 deg/s steps for speed, matching the one-count output resolution.

nodes.label: Calibrate Control
nodes.rationale: Confirm-dialog guarded control that captures the datum.

nodes.label: Saved Positions
nodes.rationale: Named position list with save, use and remove actions.

nodes.label: Export 24h CSV
nodes.rationale: Exports the last 24 hours of telemetry; the CSV first column is timestamp.

nodes.label: Duplicate app.js Script Tag
nodes.rationale: index.html includes <script src="/app.js"> twice at the end of body, so the GUI script is fetched and evaluated twice.

nodes.label: Offline Wheelhouse
nodes.rationale: Empty on purpose; fill it on a connected machine and then the whole project folder is the air-gap bundle. Install with pip --no-index --find-links=wheelhouse.

nodes.label: ARM64 Platform Wheels Required
nodes.rationale: The board is ARM64, so wheels must be downloaded with --platform manylinux2014_aarch64. Wheels built for the laptop's architecture will not install there.

nodes.label: Zephyr UNO Q Board Profile
nodes.rationale: fqbn arduino:zephyr:unoq with the arduino:zephyr platform, pinning SCServo, Ethernet 2.0.2 and Arduino_RouterBridge.

nodes.label: Arduino_RouterBridge
nodes.rationale: Required on the UNO Q for the Linux to MCU Bridge.

nodes.label: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available()
nodes.rationale: accept() hands over a connection exactly once, transferring ownership. available() returns whichever client has unread data and returns that same client again on every call, so an accept loop built on it adopts one connection into several slots and splits one HTTP request across several sockets.
nodes.norm_label: adopt connections with accept(), never available()

nodes.label: Detect Disconnects Before Accepting
nodes.rationale: Order inside Poll() matters: disconnect detection, then accept, then pump. If accept runs first a just-dropped slot can be handed to a new connection before net_close is sent, and the Linux side feeds new bytes into the old socket.

nodes.label: Edge-Triggered was_up Disconnect Tracking
nodes.rationale: Act on the was-connected to not-connected transition. Testing !connected() every pass emits net_close continuously for slots that are merely idle.

nodes.label: loop() Must Yield
nodes.rationale: Poll() returns immediately when idle so loop() spins at full speed, starving the Bridge RPC thread until servo_read misses its 10s deadline. A delay(1) at the end of Tick() costs nothing against the latency budget.

nodes.label: One Bulk Read Per Slot Per Pass
nodes.rationale: Use client.read(buffer, sizeof(buffer)), not a byte-at-a-time loop, and never block or delay() inside the pump because the same loop() also drives the servo bus.
nodes.norm_label: one bulk read per slot per pass

nodes.label: kRelayChunkBytes Must Match relay_chunk_bytes
nodes.rationale: One number in two places, bytes per Bridge message. Halving it doubles the number of Bridge round trips for identical payload; 256 is the value the working relay used.

nodes.label: Bridge Net Contract
nodes.rationale: MCU to Linux: net_open(slot, client_ip), net_rx(slot, data), net_close(slot). Linux to MCU: net_tx(slot, data), net_shutdown(slot).

nodes.label: provide_safe Registration
nodes.rationale: net_tx and net_shutdown are called from the Bridge thread while loop() may be inside the relay, so they must be registered with provide_safe. Payloads are MsgPack bin_t and must not be packed into a String.

nodes.label: Serial Works; Monitor Is Optional
nodes.rationale: The sketch prints through Serial and that is proven. Monitor (the Bridge console facade) only adds reach to App Lab over WiFi; there is no correctness reason to switch.

nodes.label: Rewriting Instead Of Porting Reintroduced Solved Bugs
nodes.rationale: The relay was once rewritten from scratch instead of ported, and the rewrite reintroduced problems the original had already solved. The reference is the Stage-2 relay sketch.
nodes.norm_label: rewriting instead of porting reintroduced solved bugs

nodes.label: Graphify-first navigation rule
nodes.rationale: A graphify query returns a scoped subgraph at a fraction of the token cost of browsing python/app/ or sketch/src/. Query before grepping; read whole files only to edit or debug specific lines. The rule is explicitly to be propagated into every sub-agent prompt.

nodes.label: Document reading flow (router)
nodes.rationale: Eight documents each answer exactly one question; CLAUDE.md is the router. BACKLOG.md is the only to-do list in the repo.

nodes.label: One fact lives in exactly one file
nodes.rationale: Duplicated facts are treated as a defect to be fixed, not as copies to be kept in sync — this is what keeps the doc set trustworthy as a substitute for reading source.
nodes.norm_label: one fact lives in exactly one file

nodes.label: Three verification commands (186 / 164 / agree)
nodes.rationale: pytest (186 tests), native make (164 checks) and check_bridge_contract.py are run before and after every change; a moved number is a stop-and-report condition.

nodes.label: Missing python/.env silently runs the simulator
nodes.rationale: Without .env, use_hardware_servo defaults to false: the UI moves convincingly while the servo never twitches. Failure is silent, which is what makes it expensive.
nodes.norm_label: missing python/.env silently runs the simulator

nodes.label: adb push never deletes
nodes.rationale: Renamed and deleted files linger on the board and get picked up instead of the new ones, so the target directory must be wiped first.

nodes.label: sshfs board mount as working copy
nodes.rationale: Edits land on the board directly, so there is no push step during development. A development convenience only, not the deployment path; the database at /home/arduino/servo_mvp.db sits outside the mount.
nodes.norm_label: sshfs board mount as working copy

nodes.label: Graphify extraction gaps (.ino and .css)
nodes.rationale: sketch/sketch.ino, sketch/tests/OnTarget/OnTarget.ino and python/static/style.css are skipped unless routed to the C++ grammar manually.

nodes.label: How to work on this repo
nodes.rationale: Read the written reasoning before rewriting; several bugs came from re-deriving solved behaviour. Never bundle unrelated changes. State what was tested versus assumed — 100% line coverage prevented none of the six AUDIT.md defects. Surface ADR contradictions rather than silently overriding.
nodes.norm_label: how to work on this repo

nodes.label: run_dev.py — dev-PC entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Exists because two imports only live on the board (arduino.app_utils, Logger461). It points DB_PATH and LOG_FILE at local files and boots the app the way main.py does, minus the Bridge relay. Console commands: overload, state, quit.

nodes.label: Bridge contract checker
nodes.rationale: Every function crossing the MCU boundary is declared twice, once in C++ and once in Python, and nothing makes the compiler or interpreter compare them. A wrong argument count compiles and imports cleanly on both sides, then fails at runtime as silence — exactly how the relay broke once. Non-zero exit suits a pre-commit hook.

nodes.label: Repository layout
nodes.rationale: app.yaml required by App Lab; python/ (app, static, tests, main.py board entrypoint, run_dev.py dev entrypoint, .env.board); sketch/; libraries/ with vendored patched Ethernet and SCServo; tools/check_bridge_contract.py.

nodes.label: The air-gapped bundle
nodes.rationale: Three parts: an ARM64 wheelhouse built with --platform manylinux2014_aarch64, the patched Ethernet/SCServo libraries, and a pinned arduino:zephyr core (0.56.0+, which adds Serial3 and the UNO Q main-thread-priority fix). Never exercised end to end.

nodes.label: Pin the Arduino core version
nodes.rationale: Board Manager does not exist on an air-gapped machine, so the target must already carry the core version built against. Stated as the most likely cause of 'it worked on my laptop'.

nodes.label: Deploy: wipe first, then adb push
nodes.rationale: adb push overwrites but never deletes. Wiping also removes .cache/.venv, so App Lab re-provisions the Python environment on the next Run; to keep the venv, delete everything except it.
nodes.norm_label: deploy: wipe first, then adb push

nodes.label: cp .env.board .env — the only manual deploy step
nodes.rationale: Forgetting it is silent: the backend runs the simulator while the UI moves convincingly. It is not shipped as .env because a dev machine holding it would try to drive hardware during pytest. Confirm the live backend via /api/v1/system/health.
nodes.norm_label: cp .env.board .env — the only manual deploy step

nodes.label: Confirm the Ethernet patch survived the first build
nodes.rationale: ~/.arduino15/internal/ is a user-global library cache shared by every app. Three or more IPAddress((uint32_t)) hits means the patch is intact; zero means App Lab re-fetched the library and it must be re-applied from libraries/.
nodes.norm_label: confirm the ethernet patch survived the first build

nodes.label: Development shortcut — sshfs mount of the board
nodes.rationale: The working copy is often an sshfs mount of arduino@192.168.1.192:/home/arduino/ArduinoApps/, so edits land on the board with no push step. Convenient for development; explicitly not the deployment path.
nodes.norm_label: development shortcut — sshfs mount of the board

nodes.label: Served from the board to any machine on the network
nodes.rationale: Operators open http://<board-ip>:8000, several at once, with nothing installed on the viewing machines.
nodes.norm_label: served from the board to any machine on the network

nodes.label: D2 — capture() can store a failed read as position 0
nodes.rationale: ZeroService.capture() calls read_raw_counts(), which is 'return self.read_snapshot().raw_counts' and discards the valid flag, so a failed read returns 0. calibrate() guards this and raises InvalidReadingError; the guard was applied to one of two paths. Preferred fix: delete read_raw_counts() from the ServoRepository contract entirely — guarding capture() alone fixes today's call site, deleting the lying method fixes every call site that will ever exist.
nodes.norm_label: d2 — capture() can store a failed read as position 0

nodes.label: D4 — Connection drops after a few commands
nodes.rationale: Reproduces with a single UI instance, so not purely a concurrency limit. Candidates: relay slot exhaustion (kMaxRelaySockets = 6 is the only limit in the system, and a single browser opens up to 6 connections per host while app.js polls continuously), or slot lifecycle bugs of the RELAY_NOTES class.
nodes.norm_label: d4 — connection drops after a few commands

nodes.label: D5 — Log output is connect/disconnect noise
nodes.rationale: Relay debug lines are ruled out (LOG_LEVEL=INFO), and the MCU is ruled out (D3). Most likely remaining candidate is uvicorn access logging, since app.js polls state continuously and every poll is one INFO line.
nodes.norm_label: d5 — log output is connect/disconnect noise

nodes.label: D7 — UI not verified on small operator screens
nodes.rationale: An iPad-class size was mentioned but the exact model was not recorded; the layout has only been eyeballed through devtools.
nodes.norm_label: d7 — ui not verified on small operator screens

nodes.label: D8 — .env must be created before the first run
nodes.rationale: A pending deploy step, not a live misconfiguration. It matters because omission is silent — use_hardware_servo defaults to False. config.py already carries a comment about being burnt by a relative env_file falling back to defaults. The database also sits outside the sshfs mount, so the stored datum could not be checked; that check is the fastest way to confirm or kill D1.
nodes.norm_label: d8 — .env must be created before the first run

nodes.label: T1 — Apply CONVENTIONS.md across the codebase
nodes.rationale: The MVP was written 'dirty' on purpose. Mechanical and high-volume, suited to an executing agent; acceptance is a zeroed gap table with 186 tests still passing.
nodes.norm_label: t1 — apply conventions.md across the codebase

nodes.label: T4 — Moves while unverified: decided, permitted
nodes.rationale: Calibration is an operator startup ritual, not a backend startup action, because the mechanism can be moved by hand while power is off. motion_service.py never consults position_verified and that stays; the site is ~3 hours away. The app.js unverified warning is load-bearing and must not be tidied away.
nodes.norm_label: t4 — moves while unverified: decided, permitted

nodes.label: T5 — Add design_diagrams/ with PlantUML
nodes.rationale: Both reference projects carry design_diagrams/pumls/; this repo is the most complex of the three — two processors, a serial bus, a relay and a browser — and has none. Minimum: an architecture diagram of the MCU/Linux split and the byte path, plus an ERD.

nodes.label: R4 — Post-MVP mechanical restraint unified under one Lock
nodes.rationale: Digital Lock, motor isolation and mechanical restraint are meant to become a single Lock concept later. Recorded so today's decisions do not foreclose it — the Lock's API and UI must not be shaped as if 'digital only' were permanent.
nodes.norm_label: r4 — post-mvp mechanical restraint unified under one lock

nodes.label: R6 — Define 'stable' by benchmark, not by adjective
nodes.rationale: Measure first, then set the bar. Agreed elements: all defects closed, T1 applied, T2 bundle booted, T3 run, R1 ceiling measured, D7 verified, D3 diagnosability, docs true; the remaining numbers come from R5.
nodes.norm_label: r6 — define 'stable' by benchmark, not by adjective

nodes.label: Current status — everything exists, nothing is stable
nodes.rationale: All three verification commands pass (186 tests at 100% line coverage, 164 native checks, contract agrees), yet eight defects are open, several observed on real hardware.
nodes.norm_label: current status — everything exists, nothing is stable

nodes.label: The bar for a delivered MVP
nodes.rationale: Other teams will judge the MVP and decide whether to procure a full project, so the bar is not 'feature complete' but stable, benchmarkable and conventionally built.
nodes.norm_label: the bar for a delivered mvp

nodes.label: Bench-verified hardware facts
nodes.rationale: 4096 counts/turn with a 44:30 belt gives 0.06 deg per count; +/-90 deg is 3004 counts and the datum must sit ~2048; a datum at 0 makes the negative half unreachable; direction +1, deadband 0, speed saturates ~1100 counts/s, acceleration has no effect above ~50; Serial1 at 1 Mbps is reliable (200/200 reads, 220 us); the Ethernet shield needs SpiRemap applied after SPI.begin() and again after Ethernet.init(); Ethernet 2.0.2 needs an IPAddress((uint32_t)0) cast patch; kMaxRelaySockets = 6 is the only connection limit.

nodes.label: Environment right now
nodes.rationale: Development runs on a WiFi-mounted board; the single servo bus adapter sits on a coloured network that cannot be introduced to the secure one, so the air-gapped path has never been exercised. This version has not yet been run on the board: no .env, no database.

nodes.label: Known gaps, stated honestly
nodes.rationale: Relay and controller have no automated coverage; OnTarget has never been uploaded; the C++ side does not log during operation; 'stable' is not yet defined by numbers.

nodes.label: D2 is the linchpin, not one bug among eight
nodes.rationale: Because moves are permitted while unverified, the travel window is the only guard against driving into a silent clamp — and the window is computed from the datum. A bad datum displaces the guard by exactly the error it exists to catch.
nodes.norm_label: d2 is the linchpin, not one bug among eight

nodes.label: ADR-0001 — Network path runs through the MCU
nodes.rationale: Production boards have the WiFi/Bluetooth chip desoldered, so the Linux side has no native network. The Ethernet shield sits on the MCU and a relay pumps bytes across the Bridge to FastAPI. The most consequential fact about the system's shape, and invisible from any one file: the sketch has no HTTP knowledge, the backend has no Ethernet knowledge, and neither reveals why the relay exists.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001 — network path runs through the mcu

nodes.label: kMaxRelaySockets = 6 is the only connection ceiling
nodes.rationale: There is no Linux-side cap at all, so payload size and connection count are architectural concerns rather than micro-optimisations.
nodes.norm_label: kmaxrelaysockets = 6 is the only connection ceiling

nodes.label: ADR-0002 — Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no framework
nodes.rationale: The binding reason is the air gap: a build pipeline means a toolchain and dependency tree that would have to be vendored and reproduced on an isolated network, for a UI of this size. Payload size over the MCU relay was secondary. Consequence: state management and reactivity are hand-rolled in app.js and must be maintained there.

nodes.label: The relay-capacity argument is unverified
nodes.rationale: It is plausible the Bridge could carry a framework's payloads perfectly well; that assumption must not be treated as established. The decision stands on the air gap regardless of how backlog R3 resolves.

nodes.label: ADR-0003 — Travel window is +/-90 output degrees, multi-turn off
nodes.rationale: Multi-turn is implemented and bench-proven but disabled. Widening the window later is two numbers in .env, not a code change, and configure_range() stays on the repository contract and runs at startup either way so the multi-turn path does not bit-rot.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003 — travel window is +/-90 output degrees, multi-turn off

nodes.label: The 44:30 belt reduction is the whole point
nodes.rationale: 180 deg at the output is 264 deg at the servo, 3004 counts, comfortably inside one 4096-count turn. The original assumption of a full 360 deg of output travel would have required multi-turn; the ratio made it unnecessary. A reader who forgets the ratio concludes the servo is barely being used.
nodes.norm_label: the 44:30 belt reduction is the whole point

nodes.label: No modulus-360 wrapping anywhere
nodes.rationale: In a multi-turn system -25 deg and 335 deg are different absolute targets a full output revolution apart, and wrapping would hide turn-count errors.

nodes.label: ADR-0004 — Repository abstraction with a simulated backend
nodes.rationale: ServoRepository is an abstract contract with SimulatedServoRepository and BridgeServoRepository; deps.py alone names either and picks on use_hardware_servo. The immediate reason was sequencing — backend, API and UI were built and tested before the C++ side existed, and that work would otherwise have been blocked on hardware. The same pattern applies to storage behind ZeroRepository and TelemetryRepository.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004 — repository abstraction with a simulated backend

nodes.label: A green suite proves only the simulated path
nodes.rationale: The stated cost of the abstraction: every defect the project has actually suffered lived in the hardware and relay paths the simulator does not exercise.
nodes.norm_label: a green suite proves only the simulated path

nodes.label: ADR-0005 — Develop as if already air-gapped
nodes.rationale: Rather than build connected and port later, the project is developed as though the air gap were in place so shipping is 'zip the folder'. The constraint is invisible in the code and explains what otherwise looks like over-engineering: the vendored wheelhouse, the patched libraries, the pinned core, and the absence of build tooling. No CDN, no package fetch, no dependency resolution at deploy time.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005 — develop as if already air-gapped

nodes.label: ADR-0006 — Bridge payloads are CSV strings
nodes.rationale: Chosen for debuggability: a CSV payload is readable verbatim in a log, which matters on a boundary where a wrong argument count compiles and imports cleanly on both sides and then fails at runtime as silence rather than an error. Declared at the top of sketch/src/BridgeApi.h and mirrored in bridge_servo_repository.py.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006 — bridge payloads are csv strings

nodes.label: Field order is a contract
nodes.rationale: tools/check_bridge_contract.py compares the two declarations and exits non-zero on disagreement — the only mechanism that catches drift, since neither compiler nor interpreter can. Snapshot field 0 is valid; discarding it is how the worst defect happened, and read_raw_counts() still discards it.

nodes.label: ADR-0007 — Moves permitted while position is unverified
nodes.rationale: _position_verified is False after every boot and the UI says so, yet the backend accepts move commands deliberately. The safety-shaped intuition to refuse them is wrong here for operational rather than technical reasons.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007 — moves permitted while position is unverified

nodes.label: Remote site makes refusal less safe, not more
nodes.rationale: Access is a three-hour drive. If the measured signal is lost the operator must recover it without dispatching anyone, and may need to drive to an externally held reference. Refusing movement until someone physically presses Calibrate converts a recoverable situation into a site visit; a system that locks itself out of the only remedy available to a remote operator is less safe. Consequences: the unverified warning in app.js is load-bearing, travel-window enforcement remains the real guard, and D1 must be fixed by making the datum trustworthy rather than by gating movement.
nodes.norm_label: remote site makes refusal less safe, not more

nodes.label: ADR inclusion criteria
nodes.rationale: A decision gets an ADR only if it is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. Failing any of the three means no ADR. Do not re-litigate: amend or supersede explicitly rather than quietly building against one.

nodes.label: Candidate ADR — how isolation, Lock and e-stop compose
nodes.rationale: Decided in principle that they stay separate controls (backlog R2, R8), but the flow between them is not designed, so the ADR is not written yet.
nodes.norm_label: candidate adr — how isolation, lock and e-stop compose

nodes.label: Single-context documentation layout
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md routes; CONTEXT.md is glossary only with no status, decisions or layout; CONVENTIONS.md holds style including undecided items; docs/ holds state, backlog, ADRs, the frozen audit and the file registry.

nodes.label: Skills must use the glossary's vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Issue titles, refactor proposals, hypotheses and test names take terms from CONTEXT.md's Language section: timestamp never ts, count never tick, datum never home, Lock never e-stop.
nodes.norm_label: skills must use the glossary's vocabulary

nodes.label: Four easily conflated position terms
nodes.rationale: Zero reference (the genus), datum (the one absolute member), baseline (whichever is active), and the servo's kLock EEPROM write-lock register which is not the Lock.

nodes.label: Open work lives only in docs/BACKLOG.md
nodes.rationale: There is no external issue tracker; the gh-based workflow once described here was never used and has been removed.
nodes.norm_label: open work lives only in docs/backlog.md

nodes.label: Why the code lives in src/
nodes.rationale: Arduino compiles src/ recursively and does no preprocessing on .cpp/.h; only .ino files get concatenated and prototypes generated. Putting logic in src/ yields ordinary reviewable C++ with real headers, namespaces and classes and no compiler magic, leaving sketch.ino as four lines handing off to App. .h files in a sketch are not auto-included, which is why every file declares its own includes.
nodes.norm_label: why the code lives in src/

nodes.label: Sketch class responsibilities
nodes.rationale: AngleConverter (counts <-> output degrees, direction sign), SignMagnitude (STS wire-format decode, the 'reads 32700' bug), ServoFaults (status 0x41 to six named flags), ServoBus (the only place touching the serial bus: retries, EEPROM unlock ritual), ServoController (the operations the backend asks for), SpiRemap (routes SPI2 to ICSP), NetworkRelay (shield <-> Linux byte pump, callback seam, no Bridge dependency), BridgeApi (the contract with Python, the only file knowing payload formats), App (composition root).

nodes.label: Header-only Arduino-free classes enable host tests
nodes.rationale: AngleConverter, SignMagnitude and ServoFaults are header-only and Arduino-free on purpose — that is what makes them testable on a development machine with plain g++.
nodes.norm_label: header-only arduino-free classes enable host tests

nodes.label: Two test tiers: host-native and on-target
nodes.rationale: They catch different things. Host-native runs constantly in milliseconds with no board, covering sign-magnitude decoding, angle round-trips within one count, the +/-90 window fitting one servo turn, direction mirroring, speed conversion and every status bit. On-target covers only what a host cannot: that the servo answers, configuration writes stick, a commanded move lands, and stop holds. OnTarget is not compiled into the main sketch because recursive compilation is limited to src/.
nodes.norm_label: two test tiers: host-native and on-target

nodes.label: TinyTest.h instead of AUnit or GoogleTest
nodes.rationale: A ~60-line harness, deliberately not a third-party framework: every dependency is a liability on an air-gapped machine.
nodes.norm_label: tinytest.h instead of aunit or googletest

nodes.label: Apply SpiRemap twice
nodes.rationale: The UNO Q routes SPI2 to D11-D13 but the Ethernet Shield takes SPI from the ICSP header (PD1/PC2/PC3). Ethernet.init() re-initialises the SPI pins and undoes the first remap, so it must be applied again afterwards or the W5500 reports 'no hardware'.

nodes.label: Drain with while, never if
nodes.rationale: The UART RX ring is 64 bytes and the socket buffers are small; one byte per loop() is not fast enough.

nodes.label: The Bridge payload contract with Python
nodes.rationale: servo_read -> snapshot CSV; servo_move 'counts,speed,accel'; servo_stop; servo_set_deadband 'counts'; servo_configure_range 'multiturn,amplification'; servo_centre_here; get_status -> 'ready' | 'no-servo'. Snapshot fields: valid,counts,moving,temp_c,volt_v,curr_a,torque_kgcm,load,status_bits. Plain comma-separated payloads are readable in a log and neither side can drift from a field order the other assumes.
nodes.norm_label: the bridge payload contract with python

nodes.label: Going live is a configuration flag
nodes.rationale: deps.py already selects BridgeServoRepository over SimulatedServoRepository on use_hardware_servo, so going live is cp .env.board .env on the board, not a code change; services, API, UI and all 186 tests stay exactly as they are.
nodes.norm_label: going live is a configuration flag

nodes.label: Nothing in src/ logs during operation
nodes.rationale: App.cpp prints a one-time setup banner and that is all; ServoBus, ServoController, NetworkRelay and BridgeApi are silent, and every defect the project has had lived in those four files.
nodes.norm_label: nothing in src/ logs during operation
